clue.text: Church split by representation of pet on a memorial

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is broken open so that other letters can sit between its two halves
a representation re-presents the given letters in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church memorial carries an image of someone's beloved pet, dividing the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a church divided over a pet's portrait; 'representation of' actually signals the anagram ENOTAP, and 'split by' means the church abbreviation is broken open around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument honouring the dead who are buried elsewhere, a kind of war memorial.

clue.text: With use of colour, Italian city's the foremost of these in stylishness

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for stylishness

parts.note: chic is elegance or stylishness
Roma is the Italian name for Rome

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: A Roman designer is the most stylish of all at using colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Note the Italian spelling of Rome is needed, not the English; 'in' signals the insertion and 'the foremost of' picks one letter from 'these'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatic means relating to or using colour, from the Greek word for colour.

clue.text: Interestingly new line on old popular composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the earlier pieces come first

parts.note: something novel is new and interesting

explanation.surface: A fresh take on an old-time songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor famous for popular songs and musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello wrote hugely popular songs such as Keep the Home Fires Burning.

clue.text: Territorials taking up dull brown coat

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up means writing it from the bottom upward, so it reverses

parts.note: drab is a dull light brown colour

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers are issued with a dull brown overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the British Army's volunteer reserve; 'taking up' turns DRAB into BARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic or coat, as worn by heralds or medieval knights.

clue.text: For most of leaf tea, straining is widely spread

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for

indicators.note: the word for leaf loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page

indicators.note: the word tea is strained, so its letters are pulled out of shape

explanation.surface: Strained tea from leaves is taken up by many people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims PAGE to PAG; 'straining' rearranges TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to spread an idea or plant widely, so it means spread far and wide.

clue.text: Prison will reportedly deal with many problems

indicators.note: something said to be reported is heard rather than read, so the clue words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: JUG is slang for prison, and 'jug will' contracted to jug'll is said like the answer

explanation.surface: A jail is said to be handling an overload of difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: JUG is old slang for a prison; JUG'LL (jug will) spoken quickly gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To juggle is figuratively to cope with several demanding tasks or problems at once.

clue.text: Judge always overturned statute, getting king dangerously cross

parts.note: ay is a poetic word for always

indicators.note: a law overturned is turned upside down, so in a down clue it is written in reverse

parts.note: a statute is a law
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A judge who always overturns the law is a danger, like a king crossing a road.
explanation.walkthrough: AY, also spelt AYE, is an archaic word for ever or always; 'overturned' turns LAW into WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaywalk is to cross a road carelessly or where it is not allowed.

clue.text: Small bird from Ghana once, not middle-of-road but extremely rare

indicators.note: one pair of letters is not used and another pair takes its place

parts.note: Ghana was the British colony of the Gold Coast before independence in 1957

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its two inner letters
a word's extremes are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A small bird from West Africa is very rare, unlike centrist politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghana was called the Gold Coast under British rule; 'not ... but' signals a swap, and 'middle-of-road' looks like politics but is just the inner pair of 'road'.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is Britain's smallest bird, a tiny songbird with a gold crown stripe.

clue.text: See river in well-judged surroundings, not like Canary Wharf

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

indicators.note: the word for well-judged surrounds the river abbreviation

parts.note: a wise decision is a well-judged one

explanation.surface: A view of the river framed by sensible planning, unlike a skyscraper district.
explanation.walkthrough: Canary Wharf is a London business district known for its skyscrapers; 'surroundings' puts R inside WISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-rise buildings have few storeys, unlike the tower blocks of a high-rise business district.

clue.text: What might give some more velocity

definitions.text: What might give some more velocity

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase more velocity are taken, a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A question about what could make something go a little faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run from the end of 'more' and start of 'velocity'; the whole clue also describes revving an engine to gain speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rev an engine is to increase its revolutions, which can give a vehicle more speed.

clue.text: Very detailed autobiography of Purcell's teacher?

definitions.meaning: an account described as such omits nothing, recounting every step in sequence
John Blow taught Henry Purcell, so his life story might jokingly be titled with his surname twice around 'by'

explanation.surface: A thorough life story written by the man who taught the composer Purcell.
explanation.walkthrough: John Blow was an English Baroque composer and organist who taught Henry Purcell; the question mark flags the punning title.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow-by-blow account is one giving every detail in order, like a boxing commentary.

clue.text: Out of control rate on Scottish alcohol abuse

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it, so the scrambled word comes after the drink

parts.note: malt is Scotch malt whisky

indicators.note: letters that are out of control run wild and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking whisky at an uncontrolled pace is a form of alcohol abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of control' signals the anagram, giving TREAT; 'on' places it after the drink, as across clues read one piece written on another.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat someone is to treat them cruelly, which is to abuse them.

clue.text: Lorry's straddling left side of carriageway where it's icy

indicators.note: a vehicle straddling something has it between its sides, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British term for a large truck

indicators.note: the left side of a written word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A heavy goods vehicle drives across lanes on a frozen road.
explanation.walkthrough: An ARTIC is British slang for an articulated lorry (a large truck); 'straddling' puts C, the first letter of 'carriageway', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is the frozen polar region around the North Pole, a byword for icy conditions.

clue.text: Trudge there reluctantly at first and run back

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the two preceding words is wanted
the word for run is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to go is to run, as a machine runs or goes

explanation.surface: Someone drags their feet on the way out and then hurries home.
explanation.walkthrough: T and R are the first letters of 'there reluctantly'; 'back' turns GO into OG.
explanation.definitionFit: To trog is a British informal verb meaning to walk wearily or plod along.

clue.text: Soup bar served up with G and T? One expects more here

indicators.note: the letters are dished up in a new order, like a meal brought to the table

explanation.surface: A drinker is served soup at a bar along with a gin and tonic, expecting more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' rearranges SOUP BAR with G and T; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub serving high-quality food, so diners expect more than just drinks and crisps.

clue.text: Keen goalie — one prepares for shooting

parts.note: being game means being willing or eager, so keen
a goalkeeper is often called simply the keeper

explanation.surface: An eager goalkeeper gets ready to face shots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'shooting' as football shots at goal; the definition means game shooting on an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamekeeper rears and protects game birds on an estate so that they can be shot.

clue.text: Famous chef offering English food that is right

parts.note: scoff is informal British slang for food
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A well-known cook serves English dishes that are just right.
explanation.walkthrough: Auguste Escoffier was the French chef who codified classic haute cuisine; SCOFF is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Escoffier is among the most famous chefs in history, author of Le Guide Culinaire.

clue.text: Unacceptable ruling about turning up

indicators.note: the word for ruling goes around the other piece

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

indicators.note: the word up is turned round, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A judge's decision on an appeal proves unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruling' looks like a noun (a court's decision) but is the adjective regnant; 'turning' signals the reversal and 'about' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant is so distasteful that it is unacceptable or offensive.

clue.text: Position taken in the House of Lords angered judges

definitions.text: Position taken in the House of Lords

parts.note: someone angered is cross
the bench is the collective term for judges or magistrates

explanation.surface: Peers in the upper chamber annoyed members of the judiciary.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament; its crossbenchers belong to no party.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbenches are where non-party peers sit, so being crossbench is a neutral stance there.

clue.text: State of monarch's no good, as some TV programmes purport to show

definitions.text: as some TV programmes purport to show

indicators.note: the letter for good is not present, so it is taken out

parts.note: regality is the state of being royal, the condition of a monarch

explanation.surface: A king's condition is poor, as seen on certain television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from REGALITY; the definition alludes to reality TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality television claims to show real, unscripted life, so programmes of that kind purport to depict the real state of things.

clue.text: Base immorality spells trouble

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a flowerbed or riverbed
evil is wickedness or immorality

explanation.surface: Fundamental wickedness leads to difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' wants to be an adjective meaning low; it is a noun, BED as a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to cause continual trouble or difficulty for someone.

clue.text: Apply pressure to carpet backing and press down firmly

indicators.note: a piece put into backing gear moves the other way, so the floor covering is written in reverse

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Instructions to push on the underlay of a rug and flatten it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'carpet backing' as a rug's underside; really 'backing' signals the reversal of a floor covering, and 'Apply ... to' joins the pressure symbol on.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to pack something down with repeated firm blows or pressure, as with tobacco or earth.

clue.text: A paper under discussion

parts.note: tissue is a thin kind of paper

explanation.surface: A document being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the one being disputed or currently discussed.

clue.text: Tie the rope, primarily, one's wanting here

definitions.text: Tie the rope, primarily, one's wanting here

indicators.note: the letter for one is lacking from the first word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter of rope is used

explanation.surface: Instructions to fasten the line, since that is what a person needs at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes I from TIE to leave TE; add THE and R, the first letter of 'rope'. The whole clue describes tying a rope as a restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope tying an animal to a fixed point, and to tether is to tie it.

clue.text: Holy ground embraced by both sides in synod

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so one piece goes within the other
both sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an acre is a measure of land, so a plot of ground

explanation.surface: Consecrated land is protected by both factions in a church council.
explanation.walkthrough: S and D are the first and last letters of 'synod'; ACRE goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred and holy are synonyms, both meaning dedicated to God or a religious purpose.

clue.text: Gift of iron bells

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
bells ring, and a ring is the sound of bells

explanation.surface: A present made of iron chimes.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is something given, such as a present or a donation in church.

clue.text: Make poor devil, dropping head, conceal his confusion

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for conceal is lost

parts.note: to cover something is to conceal it

indicators.note: the word his is put into confusion, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wicked figure, hanging its head, tries to hide its embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping head' takes the C from COVER, leaving OVER; 'confusion' rearranges HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To impoverish is to reduce someone to poverty, making them poor.

clue.text: Spring sap is flowing

indicators.note: letters that are flowing are fluid and can move into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tree juice runs freely in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is flowing' rearranges SAP; the surface reads 'Spring' as the season, but it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or a resort built around one.

clue.text: Mark my son's turned endlessly impudent

indicators.note: the two words before it are turned round, so read backwards
the word for impudent loses its final letter

parts.note: someone bold is cheeky or impudent

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their boy has become cheeky without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses MY + S to give SYM; 'endlessly' cuts the D from BOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol is a mark or sign standing for something, such as a character in writing.

clue.text: Interrupted, driving away man unfortunately rather too interested in sex

indicators.note: a word for a man is driven out of the longer word's letters before they are reused
the remaining letters have suffered misfortune and fall into a new order

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A lecherous man was cut short and sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TED (a man's name) out of INTERRUPTED to leave INTERRUP, which 'unfortunately' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having an excessive or unhealthy interest in sexual matters.
